To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the effect of anti- lymphocytic IgG in vitro upon humoral immunity is dependent upon the state of sensitization of the spleen cell population, and 2) the in vivo effect of anti- lympbocytic IgG upon humoral immunity depends upon the state of the host animal, and is dependent upon whether the host is unsensitized or sensitized to the immunizing antigen.
the anti-lymphocyte serum (ALS) inhibits both the primary and secondary humoral immune responses of the spleen cells in rats.

the effect of anti-lysocytic IgG upon the immunological (humoural) responsiveness of sensitized and unsensitized rat spleen cells in vitro and in vivo is dependent upon the presence of complement in the reaction medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of anti-lym-phocytic IgG upon the immune response.
the effects of IgG on immunological responsiveness in vivo and in vivo.
the effects of anti-lym-phocytic IgG upon the immunological reactivity of sensitized and unsensitized spleens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anti-lymphocyte globulin (ALG) is an effective suppressor of the humoral immune response.
the in vivo administration of anti-lym-phocytic IgG to unsensitized rats has no effect on the ability of spleen cells to confer primary immunological (humor-al) responsiveness.

the anti-lymphocyte serum (ALS) has a profound inhibitory effect on the immunological responsiveness of both sensitized and unsensitized spleens cells in vivo and, in addition, a significant inhibitory effect on primary responsiveness of unsensitized cells in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anti-lymphocyte serum, or its IgG fraction, has a profound effect upon the immune system, and that this effect is mediated through the action of the serum on the lymphoid cells.
in vivo and in the presence of antigen, anti-lymphocyte IgG is capable of inhibiting the expression of humoral immune responsiveness.
the anti-lymphocyte serum inhibits the immunological responsiveness of the spleen cells in a manner which appears to be independent of the immunological status of these cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of anti-CD3 on T cells is dependent on the presence of antigen.
anti-lymphocyte IgG is capable of inhibiting immunological responses.
the in vitro treatment of lymphocytes with anti-lym- phocytic serum has an inhibitory effect on their ability to transfer humoral responsiveness to recipients.
